I tried making the class small and used the same helpers but I still can't find any advantage the class might have over a good ol function

Now define public properties and methods. You end up having to re-invent some very class-like syntax.

I also personally much prefer class fields to hold instance state. Much easier to scan than imperative hooks. Also much easier to inspect in the debugger.

That's an odd comparison

In your function component, you use helpers to define the element and the template (`customElement` and `html`). But you don't in the class, so it misleadingly looks more complex.
If you did the same with the class, you'd greatly simplify the code
I do use helpers in the class actually?

Here's the props! I'll be honest, I hadn't really considered public methods until just now. I wonder if that's a common enough use case...

codepen.io/Jon-DeWitt/p...

To be sure, it's not perfect just yet, but it's still early, version 0. The goal is to make this better for typescript...

I guess the idea behind it is the important part.

Sorry I missed the `html` usage. You generally wouldn't be creating the shadow root yourself, or appending dom directly. Similar, the whole getRootNode expression wouldn't be a thing. Presumably your `customElement` helper does the first two in the function component

re: shadowRoot - That depends how conscientious you are. If you don't define it yourself, it will either be inaccessible or public.

on getRootNode - I could recreate a similar customCallback helper, but that makes very little difference. That's what it sugars down to either way.

But the comparison isn't just verbosity (although even with helpers a class is still more verbose.)

It's having everything available in the same procedural scope. No reliance on the `this` binding or implicit typing. Etc...

private props = closure variables

FP is turing-complete. That kinda thing
anything classes can achieve, functions can too, but differently. And the comparison is intended to highlight that. What advantage does the class have here?
I more meant that your helper is creating the root for you. Whereas in the class component, you do it yourself (which isn't what's common in the real world - usually a library or helper is used)
